description: We are Astro-4, a student team from Bangladesh and Global Nominees of NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. This year, we’re building FIRE HARMONIX to harmonize NASA satellite fire observations. We welcome passionate teammates skilled in GIS, remote sensing, data visualization, research, or software development who love creativity, collaboration, and solving real-world problems..
summary: FIRE HARMONIX is a transparent research prototype that makes NASA's MODIS and VIIRS fire detections comparable. As VIIRS (375 m) replaces MODIS (1 km) in the fire record, detection counts jump partly because the instrument changed, which can break the continuity of the historical record. Our pipeline keeps all original NASA FIRMS fields, normalizes brightness and Fire Radiative Power within each sensor, maps detections onto a shared 0.05° grid by day, and computes a traceable Harmonized Fire Activity Index (HFAI). An interactive dashboard offers sensor views, a burning-activity calendar, and a Scenario Lab that recalculates any score step by step, with CSV export. We also tested Isolation Forest and XGBoost and openly report that our sample was too small for reliable forecasting.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FIRE HARMONIX answers the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge. VIIRS (375 m) detects smaller, cooler fires than MODIS (1 km), so combining the two records without adjustment makes fire counts jump, and part of that jump comes from the sensor, not from the planet. We built a transparent pipeline and web dashboard that puts both sensors into one analytical frame.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Preserve: all original NASA FIRMS fields are kept; derived fields are stored separately.

2. Normalize: brightness and Fire Radiative Power are standardized within each sensor group.

3. Unify: every detection is mapped to a shared 0.05° x 0.05° grid and aggregated by day.

4. Score: the Harmonized Fire Activity Index (HFAI) combines detection activity, FRP, brightness, a sensor-agreement score and detection confidence into one score that traces back to the source observation.

The dashboard provides a 3D globe with MODIS / VIIRS / harmonized views, a Burning Activity Calendar for spotting unusual periods, a Scenario Lab that recalculates any observation step by step, and a searchable table with CSV download.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

It is deterministic and auditable: no black box, and every number can be checked. We also benchmarked Isolation Forest and XGBoost offline, and we report the result honestly: on our small sample XGBoost did not beat a simple historical-mean baseline, so we make no forecasting claim and the dashboard serves no model predictions. Our position: harmonize first, predict second.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

A FIRMS record is a thermal anomaly, not a confirmed wildfire. HFAI, its weights and the agreement score are project-defined research metrics, not NASA products. The prototype uses a small deterministic sample of NASA FIRMS data (200 observations, Nov 2024 to Jan 2025) and a documented proxy for sensor agreement; scaling needs multi-year, grid-level MODIS/VIIRS history with matched overpasses.

TOOLS

Python, SQLite, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, MapLibre GL JS, scikit-learn, XGBoost, Vercel.

USE OF AI (SI)

ChatGPT and Claude: idea development, research, script and text drafting. Antigravity and Cursor: code writing and debugging. Lovable: dashboard frontend layout. Google NotebookLM: research organization and early script. Google Flow: illustrative video clips (AI-generated, not NASA footage). All SI outputs were reviewed and edited by the team; results come from our own code run on NASA FIRMS data.

Here's a detailed video about our Project:

https://youtu.be/80RPBMgUOKg?si=woE-TtLHcp2kDnoO

TEAM

Astro-4: Ayesha, Noman, Rakin, Isteak.
